channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] Trump, Putin and Xi at one table, without Ukraine. What Moscow wants from the proposal and why Beijing might agree.
item.description: Moscow is pushing for a summit with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping to discuss ending the war in Ukraine, without Kyiv or the EU. What does Russia hope to gain, and why might China be willing to take part?

item.title: [DW] Raids at far-right group's offices at European Parliament
item.description: Authorities searched the Patriots for Europe's European Parliament offices in a long-running funding inquiry. The group says the charges pertain to its predecessor and there is "no legal continuity" between the two.

item.title: [DW] Russia arrests German man, calls him a Ukraine 'mercenary'
item.description: Russian FSB agents have arrested a German national and accused him of fighting as a mercenary for Ukraine's military. They claim he deserted over unpaid wages and say he was a sniper who once served in the Bundeswehr.

item.title: [EU Observer] Revealed: New data shows Big Tech lobbying pushing EU towards sweeping data-protection rollback
item.description: New report points to extensive industry access to European politicians, as governments back changes to data protection rules in the name of AI competitiveness.

item.title: [Financial Times] Healey to reverse cuts to cash Isa allowances
item.description: Chancellor will use Wednesday’s Budget to maintain tax-free limit at £20,000 a year, reversing plan by predecessor Rachel Reeves

item.title: [Financial Times] Healey puts UK energy reform at centre of his ‘do no harm’ Budget
item.description: Chancellor to pledge extra support for businesses, entrepreneurs and households during ‘difficult moment’

item.title: [Politico Europe] The US and Canada are talking trade. That doesn’t mean they’re near a deal.
item.description: Washington and Ottawa have intensified their discussions over the past week, but have yet to offer concessions.

item.title: [Financial Times] Washington to issue Flávio Bolsonaro US visa after election loss
item.description: Defeated rightwing presidential candidate is under investigation by Brazilian police over alleged corruption and money laundering

item.title: [Financial Times] No clear winner in Israeli parliamentary election, exit polls suggest
item.description: Gadi Eisenkot’s bloc slightly ahead of Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition, but neither forecast to secure a majority, according to TV surveys

item.title: [Euractiv] Israel opposition holds narrow edge over Netanyahu in first projections
item.description: Nationwide turnout stood at nearly 75% as of 8:00 pm, the highest in decades

item.title: [Politico Europe] Quebec’s separatist leader threatens to play spoiler at Carney’s EU summit
item.description: Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon says Ottawa would rather he “serve shrimp cocktail” at a function than stage one, and alleges a “serious lack of respect.”

item.title: [Financial Times] Washington discusses Russian deals for US oil majors in Ukraine peace talks
item.description: White House proposes renewed postwar business ties in an effort to bring President Vladimir Putin to the negotiating table

item.title: [EU Observer] Europe’s centre parties are collapsing – and, for the first time, the far-right are collaborating, rather than fighting
item.description: Opinion polling from the Pew Research Center found that 69 percent of the French population is dissatisfied with democracy, Italy 62 percent, Poland 47 percent and Spain 68 percent. All are facing upcoming elections.

item.title: [Financial Times] Putin lectures Nordic leaders on Russian history
item.description: Russia’s leader goes on extended tangent in call with western European leaders as they seek to revive Ukraine peace talks

item.title: [Financial Times] Law firm Weil prepares for possible wind-down as crisis deepens
item.description: Big Law powerhouse working with Davis Polk on options that also include last-minute merger or slimmed-down entity

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU eyes global tax deal revenue to boost next budget
item.description: European Council President António Costa is pushing national capitals to agree new EU-wide levies to finance the budget.

item.title: [Euractiv] Frontex to coordinate EU deportations, under new plans
item.description: The agency's powers would be expanded for it to oversee the bloc's deportations, with a significantly enlarged personnnel

item.title: [Financial Times] Apple hit by ‘Crackgate’ outcry over iPhone Duo screen problems
item.description: Claims of flaws in Big Tech company’s first foldable smartphone are a setback for new chief executive John Ternus

item.title: [EU Observer] Finnish president Stubb joins list of EU leaders seeking to tame Putin, in a 90-minute Kremlin phone call that caused a rift with Denmark
item.description: The Finnish-Norwegian call was "not coordinated with any of us [allies]" in advance, said Denmark's Mette Frederiksen on Tuesday - directly contradicting Finland's Alexander Stubb and Norway's Jonas Gahr Støre. "I really don't understand what these two countries think can be achieved this way," she said.

item.title: [Financial Times] The limits of hedging the AI boom
item.description: As tech investment soars, finding protection is becoming more urgent — and harder

item.title: [EU Observer] Two graphs and one map show that Russia is not currently winning the war (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,706)
item.description: Analysts tracking satellite images, daily engagements and shifting frontlines say the war has frozen into a deadly stalemate.

item.title: [Euractiv] United in animosity
item.description: Also, in tonight’s edition: Brussels squabbles over EU-Canada statement

item.title: [Euractiv] MEPs to secure funding for patient groups in next EU budget
item.description: The last-minute addition aims to ensure the funding of health NGOs

item.title: [EU Observer] EU plans massive investment in Australia’s critical minerals to cut dependence on China
item.description: Australia has announced plans to overhaul its national critical minerals strategy, and the EU says it wants to invest 'massively' in refining and processing.

item.title: [Euractiv] Russia’s diplomatic silence over Turkey-Libya maritime deal
item.description: Moscow has no comment over agreement that violates Greek sovereignty

item.title: [Euractiv] EU floats new powers for Frontex to tackle social media disinformation
item.description: Border agency could become 'trusted flagger' under EU platform rules, as bloc eyes migrant crises

item.title: [Euractiv] Lockheed to open Patriot missile maintenance facility in Poland
item.description: This should save countries 'many months' in maintenance time, the company's international chief said

item.title: [Euractiv] Europe’s energy security demands a 2040 renewables target [Promoted Content]
item.description: Europe has a winning formula. Preserving a dedicated renewable energy target beyond 2030 would strengthen energy sovereignty, support electrification, and give investors the clarity, predictability and regulatory stability needed to keep building homegrown energy.

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU prepares for a grim future with new climate-proofing law
item.description: The Commission says it's not giving up on slashing emissions but acknowledges that's no longer enough.

item.title: [Euractiv] CAP deal sparks fears farm subsidies could flow to food industry
item.description: The Commission and ministers hope upcoming negotiations will resolve outstanding issues

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] There are still more American soldiers than Western ones on Nato’s eastern border, says defence expert Robert Pszczel
item.description: Donald Trump’s 9 October diesel deal with Vladimir Putin left Europeans - including Ukraine - out in the cold, as US dollars will now become key aid in the financing of Russia's war.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Frontex soll soziale Medien auf Hinweise zu illegaler Migration überwachen
item.description: Die EU-Grenzschutzagentur Frontex soll künftig soziale Netzwerke beobachten dürfen, um Informationen über Migrationsbewegungen zu sammeln.

item.title: [Politico Europe] EIB to sign framework deal with Canada on critical raw materials
item.description: Deal marks concrete step toward closer ties between the EU and Canada.

item.title: [Euractiv] EU countries edge closer to December deal on medical device overhaul
item.description: The revision aims to reduce the regulatory burden

item.title: [Euractiv] Germany slams brakes on EU-Canada ‘associate member’ statement
item.description: Berlin's objection puts the ball back in Ursula von der Leyen's court

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU divisions persist on ‘associate member’ label for Canada
item.description: The bloc can't agree on controversial status just 48 hours before Montreal summit.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Frontex gets power to track migration talk on social media
item.description: Frontex will monitor publicly accessible social media content in a bid to stay ahead of illegal migration.

item.title: [Euractiv] Every gene in the genome: How Europe can lead the shift from treating disease to preventing it [Promoted Content]
item.description: Europe is at a crossroads. Scientific progress can help prevent disease, extend healthy lives and ease pressure on health systems. The challenge is turning discovery into patient benefit through prevention, earlier diagnosis, stronger research and coordinated action across healthcare.

item.title: [Politico Europe] French government mulled blocking social networks and mobile internet amid protests
item.description: Paris was in touch with telecom operators in the week leading up to Oct. 24 to examine ways of restricting access to social networks.

item.title: [Euractiv] Ukraine urges E5 allies to provide 10% of their air defence missile stocks
item.description: Kyiv seeks immediate air-defence reinforcements and funding to scale up domestic drone manufacturing

item.title: [Euractiv] UK, Poland deepen defence cooperation to deter Russia
item.description: The two countries will notably share expertise on their respective frigate programmes

item.title: [Politico Europe] French MPs will vote on Sánchez-style amnesty plan for undocumented workers
item.description: Presidential candidate Raphaël Glucksmann is expected to endorse the measure, which would grant amnesty to hundreds of thousands of unauthorized immigrants.

item.title: [EU Observer] Europe is in denial about war — and that’s how wars start
item.description: Europeans have not experienced war for so long that they don’t recognize it anymore, and don’t see it coming. That was also the case just before the outbreak of the First World War.

item.title: [Euractiv] Danes ‘very sceptical’ over Putin call
item.description: Finland and Norway under fire for going it alone with Kremlin contact

item.title: [EU Observer] Partial victory for disabled rights, as some carers may board flights for free from 2027
item.description: Under newly-agreed rules expected to come into force in 2027, airlines will decide whether or not companions to disabled passengers are deemed necessary for safety reasons. Only if their presence is required will their ticket be free, while companions traveling with disabled passengers anyway will have to pay for a full-price fare.

item.title: [EU Observer] Farming ministers agree on more national control of EU funds as part of CAP reforms
item.description: The bulk of EU agriculture subsidies are set to distributed via a new system of national and regional plans, as governments seize control of the bloc's subsidy scheme.

item.title: [Financial Times] US voters and Trump’s overflowing swamp
item.description: America’s affordability crisis and corruption are now treated as two sides of the same coin

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: What should we expect from the Israeli elections?
item.description: Israelis are heading to the polls today for legislative elections. It is the first national vote since 2022, and a decisive moment for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is running again.

item.title: [DW] Albania's student protests are only getting bigger
item.description: As police try to suppress anti-corruption protests by young Albanians, Prime Minister Edi Rama is claiming that "antifa" is behind the unrest. Few are buying that explanation.

item.title: [DW] Are the French police the most violent in the EU?
item.description: As protests continue in France, the French police are under scrutiny after new allegations of police brutality. The force has a bigger arsenal than most in Europe.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine: Life near the front line in Sloviansk
item.description: As Russian continues to attack Sloviansk in eastern Ukraine, thousands of residents refuse to leave or struggle to find a way out. For many, poverty, family ties and beloved pets make evacuation painfully difficult.

item.title: [DW] Bulgaria: Concerns about security in the Black Sea dominate presidential election campaign
item.description: Bulgaria's presidential election campaign has been shaped by recent drone attacks on ships in the Black Sea and the government's reduced support for Ukraine, making foreign policy a key factor in the first round.

item.title: [DW] France: Hundreds arrested after nationwide protests
item.description: The French government says more than 1,000 people were arrested following nationwide protests on Saturday. Police and elite security forces were out in force across the country as clashes broke out.

item.title: [DW] Prague honors Roma resistance fighters against Hitler
item.description: More than 1,400 Roma fought against the German Nazi occupation in Czechoslovakia. A new exhibition in Prague showcases the stories of partisans and soldiers whose fates barely received any attention for decades.

item.title: [DW] In Bulgaria, record low voter turnout triggers a November 1 presidential run-off in a poll colored by divisions over Ukraine war
item.description: Low voter turnout has triggered a run-off for the Bulgarian presidency. The vote was colored by strong divisions over Russia's war in Ukraine, and Sofia's relations with the Kremlin.

item.title: [DW] Turkey's new deal on Mediterranean maritime boundaries with Libya is exacerbating issues with Greece and the EU
item.description: Turkey and Libya plan to redraw maritime boundaries in the Mediterranean as part of a new economic corridor. This has sparked strong protests from Greece, and has also drawn the European Union into the conflict.

item.title: [EU Observer] One supply scare pushed China into renewables. Two real crises still haven’t woken Europe up
item.description: The mere threat of losing control of one maritime strait turned China into a clean tech powerhouse, while Europe, hit by two real energy shocks in a few years, is wasting time watering down its green rules.

item.title: [EU Observer] One-in-three European voters now support an authoritarian or populist party, new research reveals
item.description: A historically-high number of voters have chosen parties classified as authoritarian or populist, according to a new report analysing parliamentary election results for 260 parties in 31 countries since 1946, or since the year free elections were first held.

item.title: [EU Observer] Brazil’s Lula survives Bolsonaro scare, safeguarding EU democratic ally on climate and trade
item.description: Brazil's workers' party leader Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defied all odds to become the first president to win the second round of elections after losing in primaries. Though his adversary has failed to acknowledge defeat, EU leaders and pro-democracy groups expressed relief at the unexpected comeback.

item.title: [EU Observer] Ex-EU commissioner Reynders faces new Belgian and Polish scrutiny after EUobserver revelations
item.description: EUobserver revealed last week that a director in the Belgian intelligence service had exchanged WhatsApp messages with ex-EU commissioner Didier Reynders, which may have been part of a criminal conspiracy to block reports into Reynders' alleged wrongdoing.

item.title: [EU Observer] Ukrainian offensive creeping forward in south-east, near Velyka Novosilka (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,705)
item.description: This is where the borders of three regions meet: Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia and Dnipropetrovsk oblasts. It has received less attention in recent months because there have been more active areas of the front.

item.title: [DW] Russia's attacks on Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, are intensifying. DW asked people on the ground what life is like
item.description: Russia's attacks on the Ukrainian capital are hitting harder and more frequently, making 2026 one of the long war's bloodiest years for Kyiv. DW asked people on the ground what life is like.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine tries to shut Moscow's airports with drone strikes on Russia
item.description: Repeated Ukrainian drone attacks are increasingly disrupting operations at Moscow's airports. The pounding is part of Ukraine's plan to shut down Russia's airpace.

item.title: [DW] Serbia: Hope, tension and apprehension as voters prepare to elect new parliament
item.description: After two years of protests, Serbia faces a pivotal election on Sunday, with a student-led challenge to Aleksandar Vucic's lengthy rule. Allegations of electoral irregularities and fears of a post-election crisis abound.

item.title: [DW] Serbia: Tens of thousands rally ahead of elections
item.description: After two years of student-led protests, Serbia will soon vote in what observers describe as a referendum-like snap election pitting strongman Aleksandar Vucic against the student movement.
